text: “Untouchability” is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. The enforcement of any disability arising out of “Untouchability” shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.
source: coi-art17, the ratified text already in the archive
note: Nothing here was read off the scan. The 1957 printing sets the same words, so the archive's own text scores the reading.

text: What is more ridiculous is the teaching of the Great Shankaracharya. For it was this Shankarcharya who taught that there is Brahma and this Brahma is real and that it pervades all and at the same time upheld all the inequities of the Brahmanic society. Only a lunatic could be happy with being the propounder of two such contradictions.
source: the transcription Wikimedia Commons records for the file, which follows Writings and Speeches volume 4, pages 348 to 349
note: Commons spells the name two ways, Shankaracharya and Shankarcharya, because the manuscript does. Kept as recorded.
